question.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah is considered the father of this nation, which split from India in 1947. This nation still disputes the Kashmir province with India.
question.clue: Following its independence, this country's southern border was demarcated by the Radcliffe Line.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Din-i Ilahi.
swap.text: The Din-i Ilahi was a new syncretic religion promulgated by Akbar, the ruler of this empire. This Muslim empire ruled over most of India under its last major emperor, Aurangzeb.
swap.clue: In the 18th century, the Bengal War and the Carnatic Wars caused this dynasty to lose territory to France and Great Britain.

question.text: After he murdered Mahatma Gandhi, Godse was put on trial in the Red Fort of this Indian city. A "New" district of this city is the capital of India.
question.clue: Plans for George VI to impress the "native minds" of this city by traveling to it via plane to hold a grand ceremony at Coronation Park were dropped because of their lack of political or financial tact.

swap.leadin: In a speech after an attack by Nathuram Godse, this politician declared "friends and comrades, the light has gone out of our lives."
swap.text: Name this politician, who not even a year earlier gave his inaugural address titled "Tryst with Destiny." This politician was the first prime minister of a newly independent India.
swap.clue: His second-in-command, V. K. Menon, filibustered in front of the UN Security Council while this man's army strengthened his hold on Kashmir.

question.text: This Indian territory was returned to the Indians in 1961. The Dutch tried numerous times to conquer this territory which was named the capital of Portuguese India in 1843.
question.clue: Much later, this state became part of a union territory along with the exclaves of Daman and Diu on the coast.

swap.leadin: This Seven Years' War battle helped destroy French influence in India.
swap.text: Name this battle which saw British forces supporting the Bengalese pretender Mir Jafar rout Nawab Siraj-ud-daula's army despite being outnumbered seventeen to one.
swap.clue: It took place a year after the death of the beloved Alivardi Khan, whose nephew was killed by the son of the perfidious Mir Jafar following it.

question.text: The Kingdom of Kandy was located on this island, separated from India by the Palk strait. It was later known as Ceylon during the colonial period.
question.clue: Failing irrigation tanks triggered the Great Famine in this country's Anuradhapura Kingdom, which fell to Chola invasions.

swap.leadin: This man executed Guru Tegh Bahadur because he refused to convert from Sikhism to Islam.
swap.text: Name this ruler who defeated his brother Dara Shikoh in a civil war and brought the empire he ruled to its greatest extent. He succeeded his father Shah Jahan.
swap.clue: This ruler was denounced in an "epistle of victory," or Zafarnama, written by Gobind Singh.

question.leadin: Name these incidents during the British rule of India.
question.text: This 1930 procession to Dandi led by Gandhi was the centerpiece of a two-year campaign against a certain tax which sent sixty thousand nonviolent resisters to prison.
question.clue: Westerners were inspired by the ideology of "holding on by truth" best exemplified by this event, after which Lord Irwin agreed to lift the 1882 tax that this event protested.

swap.leadin: Name these Mughal emperors of India.
swap.text: His son Khusraw and the Sikh leader Guru Arjan both rebelled against this man, whose similarly-named son built the Taj Mahal.
swap.clue: This ruler warred over Kandahar with Shah Abbas I, whom this ruler embraces in a propagandistic miniature.

question.leadin: Name these things about an Indian dynasty.
question.text: The greatest Mughal emperor was this grandson of Babur who appeased many of his subjects by taking Hindu wives.
question.clue: This man created the syncretic religion Din-i Ilahi by drawing from elements of Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, and Christianity.

swap.leadin: This ruler reportedly chose to give up drinking before the Battle of Khanwa.
swap.text: Name this founder of an empire and father of Humayun. He defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the first Battle of Panipat in 1526.
swap.clue: This man lost control of land when he was defeated by Muhammad Shaybani.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about the Himalayan Kingdoms.
question.text: The Kingdom of Gorkha would be disestablished by Prithvi Narayan Shah in 1768. That ruler would establish this Kingdom in its place, which would last until the 2001 Royal massacre.
question.clue: Chhetris dominated this kingdom's politics, especially after the Kot Massacre reduced its king to a figurehead.

swap.text: The Rocket Corps were developed by Hyder Ali and this king, also called the Tiger of Mysore, who fought the future Duke of Wellington in a series of four wars with British colonizers.
swap.clue: The V&A owns a wooden automaton commissioned by this man of a creature biting into the neck of a Western soldier.

question.leadin: One of these objects named for the Allahabad Fort includes Late Brahmi inscriptions added by the Gupta, who built an "iron" one in Delhi.
question.text: Name this type of object which an earlier ruler topped with a statue of four lions and an abacus at Sarnath.
question.answerHtml: pillars [or columns; or pillar edicts; prompt on poles; prompt on edicts by asking “recorded on what objects?”]
question.clue: At Sarnath, a statue of four lions sat atop one of these non-rock objects which was used to display the edicts of Ashoka.

swap.leadin: One long term cause of this conflict was the Doctrine of Lapse, in which any state without an heir under the influence of the British East India Company was annexed to it.
swap.text: Name this rebellion which caused many warlords to proclaim Bahadur Shah II Emperor of India.
swap.answerHtml: Sepoy Rebellion [or Indian Mutiny of 1857; or Indian Rebellion of 1857; accept equivalents]
swap.clue: This event began after Mangal Pandey was hanged for attacking two officers.

question.leadin: This empire's power was broken after its forces, convinced that a British cavalry escort for an ammunition resupply was a flanking maneuver, retreated at the Battle of Ferozeshah (feh-roh-zay-shah).
question.text: Name this major power in the Punjab in the early 19th century, which clashed with forces of the British East India Company in two namesake wars in the 1840s. This highly militaristic empire was founded by Ranjit.
question.clue: Victories at the battles of Attock and Jamrud, among others, brought this empire to its westernmost extent at the expense of the Durrani Empire.

swap.text: The anti-Mughal alliance led by Rana Sanga is often referred to as a "confederacy" of these "princes" who ruled a number of Hindu states before the Muslim conquests of the northern subcontinent.
swap.clue: An entire ruling family of these people called the Guhilas was wiped out in 1303 after the capture of the Chittor Fort.

question.leadin: Enforced by the Viceroy Chelmsford, this legislation gave his government special "emergency powers" to censor the press, detain without trial, and arrest suspects without warrant. FTPE.
question.text: Also known as the "Black Acts," name this 1919 legislation which was passed over the unanimous opposition of the Indian members of the Supreme Legislative Council.
question.clue: The Amritsar protestors were expressing opposition to these laws, which addressed Indian sedition by removing the rights of warrant, habeas corpus, and appeal from those subject to the British Raj.

swap.text: This woman, the subject of a 520-episode docudrama on Zee TV, was a widow of Gangadhar Rao who particularly hated the Doctrine of Lapse. She rounded up an army to reclaim her annexed kingdom during the 1857 Rebellion and led a big fight, but was defeated by the Central India Force led by Hugh Rose.
swap.clue: Among the rulers of the princely states active after the fall of Maratha was this queen who died fighting the British at Gwalior Fort. Subhas Chandra Bose named his all-women regiment of the Indian National Army for this queen.
